@@

+
+  /**
+   * Request email verification by userId (alternative backend flow)
+   */
+  async requestVerificationByUserId(userId: string): Promise<{ message: string; verificationEmailSent: boolean }> {
+    try {
+      const response = await withRetry(() =>
+        this.request<{ message: string; verificationEmailSent: boolean }>('/auth/request-verification', {
+          method: 'POST',
+          body: JSON.stringify({ user_id: userId }),
+        })
+      );
+
+      return response;
+    } catch (error) {
+      ErrorHandler.logError(error, 'AuthService.requestVerificationByUserId');
+      throw error;
+    }
+  }
*** End Patch

  <section id="guards-and-authz">
    <task>Guards and how frontend should authenticate</task>
    <document title="Guards">
- JwtGuard: Accepts Authorization Bearer backend JWT or cookie appwrite_jwt; if backend JWT invalid, falls back to Appwrite JWT validation.
- RolesGuard: Requires @Roles('admin') to pass; role derived from Appwrite user labels (contains "admin" → admin).
- AppwriteAuthGuard: Only on /auth/userinfo; expects Appwrite JWT; attaches user to req.
    </document>
    <document title="Frontend auth flow">
- Preferred: Use /auth/login → store access_token (short) + refresh_token; pass access_token in Authorization.
- If using Appwrite on frontend, you can exchange session JWT via /auth/exchange-jwt or set session cookie via /auth/session for server-managed httpOnly cookie.
- For OAuth: start via /auth/oauth/:provider/start; complete via backend callback that sets cookies; then call /auth/oauth/me.
    </document>
  </section>

  <section id="dtos">
    <task>Key DTO shapes (abbreviated)</task>
    <example title="SignUpDto">
{ "email": "user@example.com", "password": "Secret123!", "metadata": { "name": "John Doe" } }
    </example>
    <example title="CreateOrderDto (orders)">
{ "title": "Site order", "description": "Business site", "total_amount": 5000000, "payment_status": "pending", "wizard_data": { "pricing": { "totalPrice": 5000000 } } }
    </example>
    <example title="WalletDepositDto">

    </example>

    </example>
    <example title="CreateInvoiceDto">
{ "order_id": "order_x", "amount": 5000000, "dueDate": "2025-09-30T00:00:00.000Z", "description": "Order invoice" }
    </example>
  </section>

  <section id="utils">
    <task>Field mapping and casing</task>
    <document title="Field casing">
- The backend stores Appwrite documents with snake_case. Some controllers serialize JSON fields (e.g., wizard_data as JSON string); frontend should treat metadata fields defensively and parse if needed.
- Reference `src/common/utils/field-mapper.util.ts` for mapping helper semantics (snake_case vs camelCase).
    </document>
  </section>

  <section id="response-shapes-and-errors">
    <task>Common response patterns</task>
    <document>
- Success: JSON objects containing `message`, domain object(s), and identifiers; payments return `authority`, `paymentUrl`, or `refId`.
- Errors: 400 BadRequest for validation; 401 Unauthorized for auth; 403 Forbidden for role; 404 NotFound.
- Email verification failure messages are user-friendly strings (e.g., link used, expired).
    </document>
  </section>

  <section id="security-and-cookies">
    <task>Cookie behaviors</task>
    <document>
- Backend may set httpOnly `appwrite_jwt` via /auth/session and `appwrite_session` and `user_info` via OAuth callback.
- Production cookies set SameSite=None; domain: `.arzansite.com`; secure true.
- Prefer Authorization header from SPA; cookie path mainly for OAuth bridge and SSR contexts.
    </document>
  </section>

  <section id="examples">
    <task>End-to-end examples</task>

{
  "steps": [

    { "GET": "{{ baseUrl }}/orders", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ACCESS" } },
    { "POST": "{{ baseUrl }}/payments/request", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ACCESS" }, "body": { "order_id": "order_x", "amount": 5000000, "description": "Order payment", "callback_url": "https://app.arzansite.com/pay/callback" } },
    { "redirect": "ZarinPal paymentUrl" },
    { "POST": "{{ baseUrl }}/payments/verify", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ACCESS" }, "body": { "order_id": "order_x", "authority": "AUTH" } },
    { "GET": "{{ baseUrl }}/receipts", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ACCESS" } }
  ]
}
    </example>

    { "GET": "{{ baseUrl }}/wallets/me/balance", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ACCESS" } }
  ]
}
    </example>
  </section>

---

- I refactored auth flows to fully use the services layer and Nest endpoints, with snake_case mapping:
  - `useAuth`: verify email now sends `token` plus `userId` to `authService.verifyEmail`.
  - `authService`: added `requestVerificationByUserId(userId)` that posts `{ user_id }` to `/auth/request-verification`.
  - `VerifyEmail.tsx`: uses `authService.requestVerificationByUserId` for resends; verification handler is memoized and the effect dependencies are corrected.
  - Replaced direct fetches in `AuthFlowTest.tsx` and `DebugApiTest.tsx` with `authService`, `invoiceService`, `receiptService`, `fileManagementService`, `siteConfigurationService`, `paymentService`, and `walletService`.

- Login/Signup/OAuth/Password Reset:
  - Login: `authService.signIn({ email, password })` is used; tokens stored via `tokenManager`; `BaseApiService` handles Authorization headers and refresh.
  - Signup: only `{ email, password }` sent; no phone/metadata, preventing phone validation errors.
  - OAuth: starts via `authService.oauthStart`, completes with backend cookies, `oauthMe` returns user; no Appwrite on frontend.
  - Password reset: `authService.sendPasswordReset` and `authService.resetPassword` used; error “Failed to store password reset token” is handled via backend; frontend shows user-friendly messages.

- Lint fixes:
  - `DebugApiTest.tsx`: wrapped helper functions with `useCallback`; eliminated dependency warnings.
  - `VerifyEmail.tsx`: memoized `handleVerification` with `useCallback` and updated effect deps. No remaining lints.

If you still get “Invalid credentials” for that email/password, please reset the password via “Forgot Password” or create a fresh account; the frontend now sends the correct payload to `https://nest.arzansite.com/api/auth/login`.
